population.text: Patients with Barth syndrome (BTHS) at least 12 years of age and weighing at least 30 kg.

citations.quote: This weight cutoff is based on the clinical trial data from SPIBA-201, which required patients to be 12 years of age and older and weighing at least 30 kg.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint family in Part 1: distance walked on 6-minute walk test (6MWT) and total fatigue score (TFS) on the Barth syndrome symptom assessment. The accelerated-approval basis was the Part 2 secondary endpoint of knee extensor muscle strength by handheld dynamometry (HHD).

citations.quote: SPIBA-201, Part 1 did not show superiority of elamipretide to placebo at the end of 12 weeks of treatment on the primary endpoint family of distance walked on 6-minute walk test (6MWT) (p=0.97) and total fatigue score (TFS) on the Barth syndrome symptom assessment (BTHA-SA) (p=0.89).

However, the Signatory Authority noted that one of the endpoints in SPIBA-201, Part 2 – muscle strength of the knee extensors assessed using HHD – could be reasonable as an intermediate clinical endpoint for accelerated approval.

n.text: SPIBA-201 Part 1 randomized 12 subjects (N=12 elamipretide, N=12 placebo across crossover periods); 10 of the 12 continued into Part 2.

result.text: Part 1 was negative on the primary endpoint family (6MWT p=0.97; TFS p=0.89). In Part 2 (open-label), median change in HHD knee extensor strength (newtons) from pre-dose baseline was 34 at Week 12, 68 at Week 24, 57 at Week 36, 41 at Week 48, 35 at Week 72, and 64 at Week 168.

citations.quote: SPIBA-201, Part 1 did not show superiority of elamipretide to placebo at the end of 12 weeks of treatment on the primary endpoint family of distance walked on 6-minute walk test (6MWT) (p=0.97) and total fatigue score (TFS) on the Barth syndrome symptom assessment (BTHA-SA) (p=0.89).

During Part 2, the median (min, max) change in HHD (measured in newtons) from pre-dose baseline (Period 1, Part 1) to Week 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, and 168, was 34 (7, 95), 68 (3, 90), 57 (9, 92), 41 (-2, 144), 35 (-4, 100), and 64 (38, 78).

indication.text: FORZINITY is indicated to improve muscle strength in adult and pediatric patients with Barth syndrome weighing at least 30 kg.

citations.quote: FORZINITY is indicated to improve muscle strength in adult and pediatric patients with Barth syndrome weighing at least 30 kg.

target_moa.text: Elamipretide localizes to and is enriched at the inner mitochondrial membrane (the site of abnormality in BTHS, where cardiolipin abnormalities from TAFAZZIN defects cause mitochondrial dysfunction), and is associated with improvements in mitochondrial structure and function.

citations.quote: Elamipretide is a new molecular entity that localizes to the inner mitochondrial membrane (the site of abnormality in patients with BTHS), improves mitochondrial structure a

Nonclinical mechanistic data demonstrated elamipretide’s enrichment at the target location, the inner mitochondrial membrane, which was associated with improvements in mitochondrial structure and function in mice with Tafazzin deficiency (the enzyme that is defective in patients with BTHS).

modality.text: Peptide (small aromatic-cationic tetrapeptide; a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder administered by subcutaneous injection).

citations.quote: FORZINITY™ is a mitochondrial cardioprotin binder indicated to improve muscle strength in adult and pediatric patients with Barth syndrome weighing at least 30 kg. (1)
Elamipretide is injected subcutaneously (SC) once daily and has no notable safety concerns other than injection site reactions and hypersensitivity reactions.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions are injection site reactions (any local administration reaction 100% elamipretide vs 67% placebo; injection site erythema 100% vs 25%). Serious hypersensitivity reactions requiring emergency medical intervention have occurred and require permanent discontinuation.

vote.text: The Cardiovascular and Renal Drug Advisory Committee (CRDAC) met October 10, 2024 and voted 10 “Yes” and 6 “No” on whether elamipretide is effective for the treatment of Barth syndrome.

citations.quote: A public advisory committee meeting of the Cardiovascular and Renal Drug Advisory Committee (CRDAC) was held on October 10, 2024, to discuss whether elamipretide is effective for the treatment of patients with BTHS.
The CRDAC vote was 10 “Yes” and 6 “No” on the question “Based on available evidence, do you conclude that elamipretide is effective for the treatment of Barth syndrome.”

basis.text: The effectiveness of elamipretide had not been established for traditional approval: SPIBA-201, Part 1 (the only randomized placebo-controlled study) did not show superiority on the primary endpoint family of 6MWT (p=0.97) and total fatigue score (p=0.89), and Part 2/SPIBA-001 could not overcome bias in effort-dependent endpoints; manufacturing facility deficiencies were also identified.

citations.quote: SPIBA-201, Part 1, the only randomized, placebo-controlled, study of elamipretide in patients with BTHS, did not show superiority of elamipretide to placebo on the primary endpoint family of distance walked on 6-minute walk test (6MWT) (p=0.97) and total fatigue score (TFS) on the Barth syndrome symptom assessment (p=0.89) at the end of the 12-week treatment period.
In addition, we identified deficiencies at the drug product manufacturing facility that will need to be resolved before this application can be approved.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Knee extensor muscle strength assessed by handheld dynamometry (HHD) in SPIBA-201, Part 2, used as an intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

summary.text: Elamipretide (Forzinity) received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 for Barth syndrome based on the intermediate endpoint of knee extensor muscle strength by HHD, after a prior Complete Response letter (May 15, 2025). It had orphan drug designation and priority review, an advisory committee (CRDAC) voted 10 Yes/6 No, and continued approval is contingent on a required confirmatory randomized controlled trial.

citations.quote: It is approved under accelerated approval pursuant to section 506(c) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) and 21 CFR 314.510, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
Elamipretide has orphan drug designation and received priority review.
